title: Optimizing MHz X-ray photon correlation spectroscopy with burst-mode free-electron laser operation
author_note: Showing the first 3 and last 3 of 25 authors
abstract: Burst-mode X-ray free-electron lasers (XFELs) provide a powerful platform for X-ray photon correlation spectroscopy (XPCS) experiments with sub-microsecond temporal resolution, but the achievable performance is constrained in practice by both photon statistics and the sample's dose tolerance. Here, we develop an analytical framework for estimating the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of pulsed XPCS measurements, including pulse-to-pulse fluctuations of the incident intensity. We combine this description with dose constraints and show that, for a fixed maximum dose, acquiring fewer frames at higher per-pulse intensity yields a higher SNR than distributing the dose over a larger number of low-intensity frames. The framework is validated against measurements at the European XFEL, where the intensity fluctuations of the investigated operation mode are found to cause only a negligible reduction in SNR. We further introduce and experimentally demonstrate a rolling bunch pattern with three pulses per train and variable pulse spacings. This scheme enables more than an order-of-magnitude increase in the accessible per-pulse intensity while maintaining equilibrium dynamics. Our results provide practical guidelines for optimizing dose-efficient MHz-XPCS experiments and for evaluating future XFEL operation modes.
subjects: Soft Condensed Matter (cond-mat.soft) ; Instrumentation and Detectors (physics.ins-det)

title: Role of antisite disorder in dictating the Ising anisotropy and ferromagnetic ground state of NdGaSi
abstract: Single-ion anisotropy and exchange interactions together set the magnetic ground state of rare-earth intermetallics, yet the role of chemical disorder on the ligand sublattice remains little explored. Here, we show that Ga/Si antisite disorder in NdGaSi stabilises the centrosymmetric $I4_1/amd$ structure and raises the Nd$^{3+}$ site symmetry to $D_{2d}$, which forbids all $m=\pm2$ Stevens operators in the crystalline electric field (CEF) Hamiltonian. Magnetization, specific heat, single-crystal neutron diffraction, and x-ray absorption spectroscopy establish the disordered structure and a collinear ferromagnetic order below $T_\mathrm{C}\approx11$~K with Ising anisotropy along $c$. A CEF analysis that fits the susceptibilities along both axes and the magnetic specific heat simultaneously yields a ground-state doublet that is $\sim97\%$ pure, in contrast to the strongly mixed ground state of the Al/Si-ordered NdAlSi ($C_{2v}$ site symmetry of Nd$^{3+}$). We argue that this ground-state purity makes the ordered moment rigid against the modulation due to frustrated exchange, selecting a $\mathbf{k}=0$ ferromagnet in NdGaSi instead of the incommensurate ferrimagnet of NdAlSi. Antisite disorder, thus, acts as a handle on CEF ground-state purity and can, thereby, select between fundamentally different magnetic ground states.

title: Gap-label bounds and optical reconstruction of Landau-subband quantum geometry
abstract: We derive a magnetic gap-label lower bound on the internal quantum weight of Landau subbands that remains nonzero even when the occupied Chern number vanishes. Using the second fundamental forms of nested subbundles to decompose the quantum geometric tensor, we isolate the constraint imposed by the uniform parent curvature and show that the excess quantum weight above the bound equals twice the weaker circular transition weight. For a noninteracting parabolic band with a periodic scalar potential, Landau-level mixing preserves the integrated relative curvature while the occupied direct gap remains open. Nevertheless, uncorrected sub-cyclotron absorption need not satisfy the projected bound. Using exact circular-dipole relations, we reconstruct the low-frequency guiding-centre weight and signed dichroism from circularly polarized absorption. This reconstruction removes the first-order orbit-polarization contribution. For an insulating filling of an isolated lowest-Landau-level-derived cluster, a potential-gradient estimate bounds the omitted remote-transition weight quadratically at weak coupling. This yields a finite-window lower bound on reconstructed quantum weight and bounds the deviation of reconstructed dichroism from the integrated relative curvature.
subjects: Mesoscale and Nanoscale Physics (cond-mat.mes-hall) ; Mathematical Physics (math-ph)

title: Normal-state exponential muon-spin relaxation and its implications for time-reversal symmetry breaking in Sr$_2$RuO$_4$
author_note: Showing the first 3 and last 3 of 15 authors
abstract: The low-temperature increase of the zero-field muon-spin relaxation rate in Sr$_2$RuO$_4$ has long been regarded as evidence for spontaneous internal fields associated with time-reversal-symmetry-breaking (TRSB) superconductivity. Here we directly test this interpretation using muon-spin rotation/relaxation ($\mu$SR) measurements on high-quality Sr$_2$RuO$_4$ single crystals. For all four samples, the onset temperature of the additional exponential relaxation in the zero-field$\mu$SR data, $T_{\Lambda}$, lies below the bulk superconducting transition temperature $T_{\rm c}$, even in the absence of applied strain. More importantly, in transverse-field $\mu$SR measurements we find a quantitatively similar exponential relaxation in a field of 80 mT applied along the crystallographic $c$ axis. This field exceeds the upper critical field of the crystals studied in transverse-field geometry and suppresses bulk superconductivity, demonstrating that the characteristic relaxation persists in the normal state. Measurements below the upper critical field reveal an additional superconducting mixed-state contribution superposed on this normal-state channel. Our results show that the zero-field $\mu$SR relaxation in Sr$_2$RuO$_4$ cannot, by itself, be regarded as a unique signature of superconducting TRSB. They call for a reassessment of a key experimental signature of TRSB in Sr$_2$RuO$_4$ and highlight the need to distinguish superconducting and normal-state relaxation channels in other unconventional superconductors.

title: Revealing the growth of structural length in glass-forming liquids without using dynamical information
abstract: Dynamical heterogeneity underlies the dramatic slowdown of supercooled liquids and has long been a central topic in glass physics. Despite considerable progress in identifying structural motifs and order parameters correlated with dynamical heterogeneity, a general characterization of structural descriptors remains elusive because they can vary among glass formers and are not generally known \emph{a priori}. To address this challenge, we establish a unified framework that can be applied to varieties of glass formers to extract structural signatures of dynamical heterogeneity directly from their static configurations. The framework combines a graph neural network (GNN) with gradient-weighted class activation mapping (Grad-CAM). Across three canonical three-dimensional glass-forming models, the resulting structural field exhibits a characteristic correlation length that tracks the corresponding dynamical correlation length. Notably, a network trained on small systems can be applied to larger systems without retraining, indicating that the extracted features are encoded in local and mesoscopic structural correlations. These results demonstrate that static configurations encode structural signatures of dynamical heterogeneity and establish a scalable, interpretable route for extracting them.

title: Chemical Programming of Stacking Order and Superconductivity Dimensionality in NbSe2-xTex Polytypic Heterostructures
author_note: Showing the first 3 and last 3 of 17 authors
abstract: Layered transition-metal dichalcogenides exhibit electronic states highly sensitive to lattice symmetry, yet elucidating the structure-superconductivity relationship has been challenging due to the lack of a continuous structural evolution within a single material system. Here, we establish NbSe2-xTex as a model system, where Te substitution drives a sequential polytypic transition across the full composition range-from the low-Te 2H phase, through mixed 1H/1T heterostructured 4H and 6R polytypes at intermediate substitution, to ideal 1T and distorted 1T' structures at high Te content. Combining comprehensive characterizations, we map both the structural evolution and the accompanying changes in spectral weight and orbital character near the Fermi level. Electrical transport measurements reveal a striking phase-dependent superconducting dimensionality: the 4H phase (NbSe1.4Te0.6) exhibits enhanced anisotropy and an anomalous boost in the in-plane upper critical field, while the 6R phase (NbSe1.2Te0.8)shows suppressed Tc (~ 2.8 K) and three-dimensional-like behavior. The combined electronic-structure and superconducting results connect the stacking sequence to effective interlayer coherence and the local spin-orbit environment. SOC band calculations resolve the distinct symmetry constraints on the 4H and 6R electronic states. These mechanisms fundamentally differ from conventional approaches by leveraging intrinsic, composition-driven polytypism to modify interlayer coupling and band structure. Thus, by establishing a definitive phase diagram that directly correlates polytypism with superconducting dimensionality, our work provides a clear roadmap for the rational design of low-dimensional superconducting devices through stacking-sequence engineering.

title: Recoverable Necking Enabled by Reverse Phase-Boundary Motion in Liquid Crystal Elastomers
abstract: Strain localization is often associated with plastic flow and permanent deformation. Here we show that a tensile neck in a crosslinked nematic network can undergo nearly complete recovery through reverse phase-boundary motion, leaving little residual deformation. In a monodomain liquid crystal elastomer stretched perpendicular to its initial director, this recovery occurs during an isothermal loading-unloading cycle. Digital image correlation resolves the process as the retreat of interfaces separating low- and high-stretch regions, where the high-stretch domain shrinks while previously necked material thickens, despite substantial mechanical hysteresis. Within the recoverable-necking regime, increasing temperature lowers the loading plateau stress but raises the unloading plateau stress. A nonconvex constitutive description provides an energetic basis for the coexistence of the two stretch states, while gradient regularization accounts for the finite width of their interfaces through an equilibrium reference profile. These results identify the spatial mechanism of neck recovery and distinguish recoverable strain localization from mechanical reversibility in an orientationally ordered polymer network.

title: Ultraslow vorticity modes in colloidal fluids
abstract: In the conventional unsteady-Stokes picture, vorticity generated by a transient disturbance relaxes rapidly through viscous diffusion once the forcing ceases. This view presumes a quiescent solvent. In colloidal and biological fluids, thermal motion continually perturbs the surrounding fluid, raising a natural question: can equilibrium fluctuations, mediated by hydrodynamic coupling, sustain vorticity over mesoscopic scales and times? Here, using high-speed confocal microscopy of moderately dense colloidal suspensions, we reconstruct the conditional mean hydrodynamic response to Brownian displacements of prescribed magnitude and direction. We find a long-lived, spatially structured vorticity field that decays far more slowly than predicted by unforced unsteady-Stokes dynamics. A coarse-grained phenomenological model based on fractional Brownian motion, constrained by independently measured single-particle subdiffusion, quantitatively captures its temporal and spatial decay. These findings reveal a field-level manifestation of hydrodynamic memory in fluctuating low-Reynolds-number flows, with implications for transport and collective dynamics in complex fluids.
comments: 8 pages, 3 Figures (To appear in Phys. Rev. Lett. (2026))

title: Kinetic Arrest of a Disordered First-Order Phase Transition in Strained V2O3 Thin Films
abstract: We develop a continuum phenomenological theory for the kinetic arrest (KA) of a first-order phase transition (FOPT), taking the thermal and electric field-driven metal-insulator transition (MIT) in epitaxial V2O3 thin films as a prototype. By defining a coarse-grained mesoscopic order parameter representing the metallic volume fraction coupled to the primary structural monoclinic distortion, we formulate a Time-Dependent Ginzburg-Landau (TDGL) framework integrated with a non-local elastic interaction kernel and an Imry-Wortis quenched disorder landscape. We derive an explicit dynamic criterion for the kinetic arrest boundary TK(E) by analyzing the divergence of the intrinsic order-parameter relaxation time relative to experimental observation timescales. Our framework rigorously decouples the thermodynamic driving force from the kinetic activation barrier. We demonstrate that epitaxial substrate-induced clamping elevates local elastic barriers, pinning domain boundaries and stabilizing an arrested, inhomogeneous mosaic of metallic and insulating phases down to cryogenic temperatures. The simulated transformation kinetics exhibit an Avrami exponent suppression to values n < 1, reflecting slow, hindered domain-wall propagation. Furthermore, we examine the effect of an external electric field as an isothermal mechanism that lowers this kinetic barrier, providing a phenomenological description of threshold de-arrest and multi-level resistance states. We critically discuss this electronic barrier-lowering mechanism in comparison with electrothermal Joule heating, establish diagnostic criteria to distinguish them, and contextualize these non-equilibrium dynamics with related phenomena in disordered superconducting films.

title: Growth and anisotropic directional dependent transport properties of Altermagnetic CrSb
author_note: Showing the first 3 and last 3 of 10 authors
abstract: CrSb is a metallic altermagnet exhibiting large momentum-dependent spin splitting and antifer- romagnetic ordering well above room temperature. Although its electronic and magnetotransport properties have attracted considerable attention, a systematic comparison of crystals prepared us- ing different growth methods remains limited. Here we investigate the structural, magnetic, and anisotropic transport properties of CrSb single crystals grown by Sb(self)-flux, Bi flux, and chem- ical vapor transport (CVT). Each of these growth reveals distinct crystal morphologies. Magne- tization measurements exhibit broadly consistent antiferromagnetic responses, with an additional low-temperature contribution observed in Bi-flux-grown crystals. All samples display metallic resis- tivity and positive, nonsaturating magnetoresistance up to 9 T. Sb-flux- and CVT-grown crystals exhibit comparable residual resistivity ratios and magnetoresistance, whereas Bi-flux-grown crys- tals show enhanced residual resistivity and a substantially reduced magnetoresistance, consistent with stronger carrier scattering. Hall measurements reveal a pronounced dependence on the field- current configuration, including nonlinear field dependence and opposite Hall polarities for different crystallographic orientations. These results establish the reproducibility of anisotropic magneto- transport across distinct growth routes while highlighting the sensitivity of carrier scattering to crystal-growth conditions. Our findings provide a comparative framework for selecting CrSb single crystals for orientation-dependent transport and spintronic investigations.

title: Unveiling plastic rearrangements in silica glass through persistent homology
abstract: Plastic deformation of amorphous solids proceeds through localised atomic rearrangements. While much effort has been devoted to identifying where such rearrangements occur, how the local structure changes during a rearrangement is less well understood. In silica glass, a rearrangement can involve both distortion within SiO4 tetrahedra and deformation of the network connecting them, but the contributions of these two modes have rarely been quantified. Here, we characterise plastic rearrangements in silica glass under athermal quasistatic shear using persistent homology, which extracts rings from atomic configurations, and link the changes in the persistence diagrams to individual rings in real space. We classify rearrangement events into two types according to bond-coordination changes. By performing inverse analysis, we reveal that Si-centred triangles within tetrahedra, hinge triangles spanning two corner-sharing tetrahedra, and the other (non-hinge) O3 triangles are the dominant sources of topological changes upon rearrangements. The birth-time changes of Si-centred and hinge triangles closely follow the change in the angle opposite the longest edge, whereas that of non-hinge triangles also reflects changes in inter-tetrahedral O--O distances. Further, we clarify that triangles with large birth-time changes are localised in the rearrangement region. Comparing the two types of triangles, we find that the ratio of their birth-time changes is larger for coordination-changing events than for coordination-preserving events, indicating that such events involve relatively more intra-tetrahedral deformation compared with network deformation. These results demonstrate that persistent homology separates intra-tetrahedral and network deformation and quantifies each as a continuous quantity within a single framework.
subjects: Soft Condensed Matter (cond-mat.soft) ; Disordered Systems and Neural Networks (cond-mat.dis-nn)

title: Majorana quasiparticles, mass hierarchies, and the phase diagram of the Gross-Neveu model in D=2+1
abstract: We show that the canonical $2+1$-dimensional $O(2N)$-symmetric Gross-Neveu model with the inversion-breaking mass-term features a sequence of $O(2N-k) \times O(k)$ - symmetric ground states in its zero-temperature phase diagram, with $k=1,...,N$. For odd $k$ the quasiparticle excitations are itinerant, massive, two-real-component Majorana fermions, i.e. half of Dirac fermions. The solutions of the mean-field equations symmetric under $O(2N-k_1-k_2) \times O(k_1) \times O(k_2)$ with $k_1, k_2 \geq 1$ also exist, but are found to be unstable. Some manifestations of Majorana quasiparticle in the particular ``uniaxial nematic" state with $k=1$ are outlined, and analogies to other physical systems are offered.
subjects: Strongly Correlated Electrons (cond-mat.str-el) ; Statistical Mechanics (cond-mat.stat-mech); High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

title: Artificial Spin-Glass of Antiferromagnetic Co3O4 Nanocubes Using Spin-Polarized Oxygen
author_note: Showing the first 3 and last 3 of 8 authors
abstract: Preferentially exposing (100) surface terminations of Co$_{3}$O$_{4}$ using cube-shaped nanoparticles yields an unconventional rearrangement of ions that generates spin-glass-like magnetism from the antiferromagnetic nanocubes. The necessary magnetic frustration arises out of competition between polarized Co-O bonds from charge transfer between O 2p and Co 3d orbitals, and highly anisotropic Co$^{2+}$ ions combined with anomalous high spin Co$^{3+}$ ions in octahedral sites. Size control permits tuning this novel combination of ions via preferentially polarizing Co-O bonds. The presence of control over frustrated magnetism among antiferromagnetic nanocubes yields an artificial spin glass platform for exploring unconventional nanomagnetism and engendering new opportunities for emerging technologies like spintronics and physical reservoir computing.
subjects: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci) ; Disordered Systems and Neural Networks (cond-mat.dis-nn); Mesoscale and Nanoscale Physics (cond-mat.mes-hall)

title: Geometric Contribution to the Electron-Phonon Coupling Constant: Checkerboard and Hyper-diamond Models
abstract: Recent theoretical studies on electron-phonon coupling (EPC) - a key ingredient in the emergence of diverse quantum phases such as superconductivity and charge-density waves - have revealed a distinct contribution to its strength arising from the quantum geometry of electronic bands. Here we investigate the quantum geometric contribution, characterized by the quantum metric, to the dimensionless EPC constant in the checkerboard and hyper-diamond models, under the Gaussian approximation. We show that in the checkerboard model, the geometric contribution can be tuned independently while keeping the energetic part fixed, demonstrating the possibility of enhancing EPC strength through quantum geometry. In the hyper-diamond model, the geometric contribution accounts for roughly $50\%$ of the total EPC constant across all spatial dimensions, generalizing the $d=2$ result for graphene to higher dimensions.

title: Simple Routes to Turing-Like Patterns
abstract: Spots, stripes, and networks recur in systems with very different microscopic dynamics, suggesting that the competing processes behind Turing-like patterns may be easy to realise. We ask whether local amplification coupled to suppression over a wider region can generate these geometries in simple systems beyond chemical reaction--diffusion models. We test this idea in two settings, a binary cellular automaton obtained by adding a distant neighbour count to Conway's Game of Life and a self-gravitating toy universe described by particle motion and two continuous fields. The automaton produces spots, stripes, and coexistence across its control plane, while a rule retaining only the two opposing counts produces islands, stripes, and holes. Directional correlations and intrinsic dimension identify the same region of orientational order. In the gravitational system, convergence increases local density while mass transport depletes the surroundings. The two-field and particle densities have a smoothed spatial correlation of $0.962$ at scale factor $a=1$ under the original force law, and strengthening its long-wavelength component drives both descriptions toward fewer dense condensations. Together, these results show how simple counting rules and redistribution of a conserved quantity can realise competing growth and suppression, providing two concrete routes by which Turing-like geometries can recur across different dynamics.
subjects: Statistical Mechanics (cond-mat.stat-mech) ; Pattern Formation and Solitons (nlin.PS)

title: Tuning the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction in CoFeB thin film heterostructures
author_note: Showing the first 3 and last 3 of 7 authors
abstract: The Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya Interaction (DMI) is essential for stabilizing chiral spin textures in spintronics, yet achieving consistent quantitative measurements across different techniques remains a significant challenge. Heterostructures consisting of magnetic thin films sandwiched between non-magnetic heavy metals have been shown to possess substantial DMI; however, these vary in both magnitude and handedness for supposedly identical samples, indicating the sensitivity of DMI to both interfacial properties and measurement techniques. Here, systematic tuning of the DMI in ultra-thin magnetic heterostructures of Pt/CoFeB/Ta/Pt is achieved by varying the thickness of a tantalum sub-monolayer with thicknesses ranging from $0.1\,\mathrm{nm}$ to $0.4\,\mathrm{nm}$. The magnitude and sign of the DMI are measured using three independent methods: the parallel stripe domain model, edge nucleation field analysis, and Brillouin light scattering. The three independent approaches reveal excellent agreement within the experimental error. This ability to controllably tune and reliably quantify DMI provides a viable route toward engineering chiral magnetic textures, including domain walls and skyrmions, for next-generation spintronic devices. The necessity for precise measurements of magnetic parameters and careful attention to detail are discussed because calculations of the DMI for each technique depend on different parameters.

title: Geometric properties of Wilsonian flows of periodic potentials in two dimensions
abstract: Periodic interactions can possess multiple competing minima and barriers, whose evolution under coarse-graining offers a geometric perspective complementary to the scaling of Fourier harmonics. We study this evolution in two dimensions by deriving a functional Wilsonian renormalization-group flow for a general smooth periodic potential and its running sine-Gordon frequency within a constant-kinetic projection. Reaction--diffusion and Burgers representations reveal two key properties of the flow: discrete translation symmetries are preserved, and the number of extrema can only remain constant or decrease. Consequently, the nonlinear generation of Fourier harmonics may accompany a progressive simplification of the potential landscape. We illustrate the role of symmetry with two complementary examples. A weak breaking of the $\pi$-translation symmetry allows a reduction from four extrema to two, whereas a non-sinusoidal interaction retaining this symmetry evolves from eight extrema to the four protected by its periodicity. These results highlight how symmetry and coarse-graining jointly reorganize competing minima and barriers in periodic interactions.

title: Atomic layer etching of niobium via alternating O$_2$ and H$_2$/SF$_6$ plasma exposures
abstract: Niobium thin films are a key component of superconducting detectors and electronics, and film surface quality, surface roughness, and geometrical dimensional accuracy affect many performance metrics. Atomic layer etching (ALE) is of interest for modifying film surfaces owing to its Angstrom-scale etching precision and surface smoothing characteristics. Here, we report a plasma-enhanced ALE process for Nb based on sequential O$_2$ plasma and H$_2$/SF$_6$ plasma exposures. The process achieves an etch per cycle of 5-7 Angstrom/cycle and exhibits surface smoothing. The superconducting transition temperature of the ALE-treated films is maintained up to the expected decrease associated with reduced film thickness. Our ALE process could find applications in superconducting electronics for which surface quality and precise thickness control are of high importance.

title: Large deviations, effective dynamics, and dynamical phase transitions in random maps
abstract: Large deviation theory provides a natural framework to characterize rare fluctuations of time-averaged observables in deterministic and stochastic systems. Building on previous results for deterministic chaotic maps, here we extend the Doob transform to random maps, constructing an effective dynamics in which rare events become typical. This makes it possible to directly reproduce the dynamics of rare trajectories that are exponentially difficult to sample under the original dynamics. We further apply spectral large-deviation methods to characterize dynamical phase transitions in random maps. The spectral structure of the tilted operator provides insight into the mechanisms underlying these transitions and, in particular, allows us to identify the appropriate initial states that select one dynamical phase or another. Our results extend the connection between large deviation theory, spectral methods, and effective dynamics to random chaotic maps, providing a general framework to study rare events and dynamical phase transitions in these systems.
subjects: Statistical Mechanics (cond-mat.stat-mech) ; Mathematical Physics (math-ph); Chaotic Dynamics (nlin.CD)

title: Topological phases protected by half-chiral symmetry
abstract: Chiral (or sublattice) symmetry describes bipartite systems such as the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) chain where same-sublattice A-A and B-B hoppings are forbidden, enabling the protection of topological phases. Here we identify new topological phases protected by half-chiral symmetry wherein chiral symmetry is preserved on only one sublattice, as may occur with sublattice imbalance (e.g. graphene-hBN) or localized orbitals (e.g. zincblende). Unlike conventional symmetry operators described by group theory, half-chiral symmetry is an algebraic constraint on the sublattice-projected Hamiltonian such as $PHP=0$, requiring a new framework for topological protection. We develop such a framework, identifying real-space bulk topological invariants and corresponding topological boundary modes that stick to zero energy. In two dimensions we construct a half-chiral Kekule honeycomb model and show that its unusual higher-order topology protects a single zero-energy mode at a single corner.
subjects: Mesoscale and Nanoscale Physics (cond-mat.mes-hall) ; Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci); Strongly Correlated Electrons (cond-mat.str-el); Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

title: Topologically Obstructed Kondo Hybridization: A Route to Kondo Semimetals
abstract: The interplay of strong correlations, topology, and symmetry can reshape the low-energy electronic structure of quantum materials and drive the emergence of novel quantum phases. In heavy-fermion systems, the Kondo effect entangles localized $f$ moments with conduction electrons, giving rise to coherent heavy-electron bands at low temperatures, typically characterized by a Kondo hybridization gap. Here we show, however, that the topology and symmetry of the conduction-electron Fermi surface can obstruct the opening of the Kondo hybridization gap at certain momenta. Treating the Fermi surface of a three-dimensional system as an effective two-dimensional manifold, we demonstrate that nontrivial topological invariants defined on this manifold impose a topological obstruction to opening a full hybridization gap, forcing the $fc$ hybridization to vanish at certain momenta on the Fermi surface. These hybridization zeros lead to crossings between $c$ and $f$ bands, giving rise to nodal points or lines near the Fermi energy within the Kondo phase. Our results establish topological obstructions to Kondo hybridization as a route to Kondo semimetals, revealing a fundamental connection between Fermi-surface topology and the emergence of correlated electronic phases.

title: Structure and relaxation of long-lived odd-parity modes in two-dimensional Fermi liquids
abstract: In two-dimensional Fermi liquids, odd-parity deformations of the Fermi surface relax anomalously slowly at a rate $\sim T^4$, where $T$ is the temperature. However, the leading-logarithmic prediction for the magnitude of this rate $\sim m^4 \ln m$, where $m$ is an angular harmonic index, exceeds exact-diagonalization results and the $\ln m$ scaling is not observed. We resolve this discrepancy by evaluating the 2D Fermi-liquid collision integral for general regular isotropic potentials to leading order in $T/T_F$, including the nonlogarithmic term beyond the $\ln(T_F/T)$ term. We find that the local temperature modulation of the odd mode, which we call the thermal dressing, suppresses relaxation by collinear scattering, with residual relaxation set by large-angle scattering. Such large-angle processes give corrections of order $\ln m/\ln(T_F/T)$ that are not small and must be resummed. We benchmark our results against exact-diagonalization calculations for constant interactions and find agreement over a range $m^2 T/T_F \lesssim 0.4$, and we provide closed-form results for the slowest odd-mode relaxation rate of a spin-polarized dipolar gas.
subjects: Mesoscale and Nanoscale Physics (cond-mat.mes-hall) ; Quantum Gases (cond-mat.quant-gas); Strongly Correlated Electrons (cond-mat.str-el)

title: Shift current as a stacking spectroscopy of hexagonal boron nitride multilayers
abstract: Out-of-plane polarization can be tuned by sliding polar monolayers in van der Waals materials; the bulk photovoltaic effect is emerging as a natural optical probe, provided the photocurrent tracks the polarization. We test that assumption by computing the polarization and the shift-current tensor from first principles across the stacking landscape of bi-, tri-, and tetralayer hexagonal boron nitride. The two quantities share one robust property: the vertical response reverses with the polarization while the in-plane one does not. Beyond this rule, the correspondence must be read with caution: stackings with identical polarization carry vertical monochromatic photocurrents of opposite sign; the spectra reorganize and even reverse sign at some photon energies along a constant-polarization plateau; and the strongest vertical peak of the entire pathway sits where the polarization crosses zero. The reason is structural: the polarization counts polar interfaces, while the shift current reads their positions. Broadband illumination reads the domain sign; monochromatic photocurrent maps can read the stacking registry. In a sliding ferroelectric, the bulk photovoltaic effect can operate as a stacking spectroscopy.
subjects: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci) ; Mesoscale and Nanoscale Physics (cond-mat.mes-hall)

title: Capillary partitioning of solutes on conformally coated colloidal monolayers: a universal geometric threshold
abstract: Depositing a conformal solid film on a hexagonal monolayer of spheres progressively closes the interstitial pores, and this closure controls where a dilute solute spin-coated from a volatile solvent ends up after drying: buried in the interstitial valleys or spread over the exposed caps. We derive the fraction of solute that ends in the valleys from first principles, for any sphere radius, film thickness and wetting liquid. The control parameter is the film thickness divided by the sphere radius, and a purely geometric threshold, about 0.155, separates two regimes for all sphere sizes. Below it, the three-sphere interstice is an open cup that the liquid fills through a narrow throat at the sphere equator, and about nine tenths of the solute end in the valleys. Above it, the throat pinches shut, sealing the cup and leaving only a shallow surface dimple, so this fraction drops more than twofold, never to recover. Treating the throat as a nearly triangular duct gives a closed-form filling rate, confirmed by exact flow calculations. During spin-coating, filling outpaces drying by up to five orders of magnitude, except within a fraction of a nanometre of the threshold. Partitioning is therefore set by capacity alone, through a one-parameter ratio of exact void volumes, identical for all sphere sizes. Thin-film simulations confirm the direction of liquid transport. For dye in ethanol on tantalum-pentoxide-coated polystyrene lattices, the predicted on-cap fraction rises from 0.06 to 0.76 across the threshold, agreeing at both ends with values inferred from measured Purcell factors.

title: Quantum effects on the Peierls stress for screw dislocations in α-Fe
abstract: The large discrepancy between the Peierls stress calculated using atomistic methods and that measured in experimental studies is well known. Despite significant research efforts over the past decades, our understanding of this mismatch remains limited. This work presents a multiscale study on the kinetics of screw dislocations in {\alpha}-Fe at 0.7K, employing the phonon description of temperature and using the Concurrent Atomistic-continuum (CAC) method as the simulation tool. Our simulations are shown to preserve the Bose-Einstein distribution of phonon modes and reproduce the nucleation and propagation of kink pairs. Large-scale CAC simulations with dislocation line lengths ranging from 0.1 to 2.1 microns, a typical range of lengths for screw dislocation lines, are performed, providing a quantitative and mechanistic understanding of the phonon-dislocation in {\alpha}-Fe. The experimentally measured Peierls stress in {\alpha}-Fe has been successfully reproduced, and the quantum effects on Peierls stress are quantified. Dependencies of phonon-dislocation interactions on dislocation line length and specimen size are explored and discussed.
